scope: Metadata-only provenance check for the BDI Muha and Ntahangwa target identity discrepancy. No geometry was acquired or inspected.

definitions.boundaryYearRepresented: The year or range of years which the boundary layers represent.
definitions.sourceDataUpdateDate: The date source information was integrated into the geoBoundaries repository.
definitions.buildDate: The date the source data was most recently standardized and built into a geoBoundaries release.

official_documentation.implication: Repository integration/build dates must not be substituted for boundaryYearRepresented.

metadata.boundarySource: New York University Spatial Data Repository, Stanford University, Map Maker Limited

metadata_lfs_pointer.body_status: Retrieved by a bounded ordinary GET after the sandbox's first DNS-only failure; actual bytes verified against the pinned SHA-256 and size.

parent_metadata_lfs_object.body_status: Retrieved and verified by the same bounded method.

authenticated_parent_to_release_field_di.interpretation: The value-level metadata change is only a buildDate update. It does not revise the represented year or identify a target-specific geometry/member change.

gbOpen.specific_feature_result: No dated or target-specific publisher explanation found for retained feature IDs 21766830B84199363749171 (Muha) or 21766830B87038696970617 (Ntahangwa). Existing retained 119-feature source properties contain no per-feature date or predecessor lineage.

metadata.boundarySource: UN SALB, Institut Geographique de Burundi

gbAuthoritative.assessment: This is a distinct, later-dated source family from gbOpen (different layer ID, source organizations, and license). Its 2015 represented interval makes it a potentially relevant independent provenance source, but layer-level metadata alone does not establish that either retained feature ID corresponds to Muha/Ntahangwa, or that its polygons are compatible with the original target geometry. The UN SALB terms apply; any later comparison must respect them. No authoritative geometry was acquired.

conclusion: Publisher material confirms a genuine 2007-versus-2015 source-family distinction but does not explain the two retained gbOpen feature IDs. The 2023 date denotes repository integration/build, not represented vintage. The gbAuthoritative layer is a plausible target-specific follow-up source, not proof by name, level, or 119-unit count.
